latest.title: Completion of Disposal
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 0940P
Sound Energy PLC
04 August 2026
4th August 2026
Sound Energy PLC
​
("Sound Energy", the "Company" and together with its subsidiary undertakings the "Group")
Completion of the Disposal of Sound Energy Meridja Limited
and Relinquishment of Arran Energy Exploration Interests
Sound Energy PLC (AIM:SOU), the AIM quoted transition energy company, is pleased to announce that following shareholder approval and the fulfilment of outstanding conditions precedent it has now completed the sale of Sound Energy Meridja Limited ("SEML") to Managem SA ("Managem"), which was previously announced on 26 May 2026 (the "Disposal").
The Company's subsidiary, Arran Energy Holdings Limited ("Arran"), has also relinquished its 27.5% interest in the Anoual Exploration Permit and has waived its rights in the Grand Tendrara Exploration Permit.
The Company received cash proceeds of US$57 million (prior to working capital adjustments) which will be utilised to repay all of its outstanding debt, including its Eurobond liabilities on the terms announced on 12 June 2026. Following settlement of all of its balance sheet liabilities, the Company is expected to have a cash balance of circa US$11 million.
The strengthened balance sheet provides the financial flexibility to pursue disciplined, cash-generative acquisition opportunities in the renewable and hydrocarbon energy transition space and is expected to improve the Company's access to both the equity and debt capital markets. Alongside this acquisition strategy, the Company will continue to develop in Morocco, Tayra, its solar power platform, and HyMaroc, its hydrogen and helium exploration business.
Majid Shafiq, Chief Executive Officer, commented:
"Today's announcement is much more than the completion of a transaction. It marks the successful execution of the plan we set out in May and gives Sound Energy the platform to move into the next phase of its growth. Our focus now is on execution. We have capital to invest, a clear investment strategy and are already evaluating opportunities that can build a larger, diversified and cash-generative energy business. At the same time, we remain committed to developing our existing businesses in Morocco. I believe we now have the financial strength and flexibility to deliver on our strategy.
I would also like to thank our partner, Managem, for the excellent working relationship we have built over the last two years and for their collaborative approach in bringing this transaction to a successful conclusion. We wish them every success in the continued development of the Tendrara project."

PDMR Dealings, Exercise of Options and Total Voting Rights
Sound Energy, the AIM-listed transition energy company,
announces
that Graham Lyon, Non-Executive Chair, on 23 June 2026
purchased a total of 603,093 ordinary shares of £0.001 each in the Company ("Ordinary Shares") at an average purchase price of £0.020724 per share in the Company.
The Company also announces
that Mr Lyon exercised nil-cost options over 774,094 Ordinary Shares.
The Company has therefore issued to Mr Lyon a total of
774,094
new ordinary shares of £0.001 each in the Company ("New Ordinary Shares"), pursuant to the exercise of options.
As a result of the above transactions, which are detailed in each PDMR Notification Dealing Form below, Mr Lyon's interest in the Company is 2,078,413 Ordinary Shares, representing 0.91% of the issued share capital.
Application has been made for the admission of the New Ordinary Shares to trading on AIM ("Admission"). The New Ordinary Shares will rank pari passu with the existing Ordinary Shares and it is expected that Admission will become effective on or around 8.00 a.m. on or around 29 June 2026.
Following Admission, the Company's issued share capital will consist of 226,928,560 Ordinary Shares of £0.001 each with voting rights in the Company and 2,180,000 Sanctioned Holding Shares of £0.01 each totalling 229,108,560 Ordinary Shares with voting rights. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in treasury. This figure of 229,108,560 may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they require to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the share capital of the Company under the UK Financial Conduct Authority's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.
The Company notes that 2,180,000 ordinary shares in the Company (prior to the Share Capital Reorganisation announced on 10 February 2026) (the "
Sanctioned Shares
") are held by a shareholder who is currently subject to applicable sanctions (the "
Sanctioned Shareholder
"). While the Sanctioned Shareholder remains subject to such sanctions, the Board has taken the view that the Company should not recognise the exercise of voting rights attaching to the Sanctioned Shares.
If, in due course, the Sanctioned Shareholder ceases to be subject to applicable sanctions (or the relevant restrictions otherwise no longer apply) , the Board currently intends to propose an appropriate resolution at the Company's next Annual General Meeting (or, if the Board considers it necessary or appropriate, at a general meeting) to seek shareholder approval to implement the Share Capital Reorganisation in relation to the Sanctioned Shares as the Sanctioned Shares were excluded from the Share Capital Reorganisation. Any such proposal would be announced separately in due course.

company_30s.what_they_do: SOU.L is an AIM‑listed energy exploration firm that has historically focused on oil and gas assets in Africa and the Middle East. The company has been active in drilling and exploration, but it has recently sold off non‑core assets to streamline operations.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The firm sits in a niche market where small, nimble operators can capture new upstream opportunities that larger majors overlook. Its ability to secure low‑cost access to untapped fields could give it a competitive edge if the sector rebounds.
company_30s.current_state: SOU.L is currently in a restructuring phase: it has sold a key asset (SEML), completed a bond restructuring, and is pivoting its focus to a new partnership with Georgina Energy. The company is still cash‑burning, but the recent asset sales and debt relief suggest a fresh start. The share trades at a price that reflects a steep discount to any realistic valuation.

rns_narrative: The company is shedding non‑core assets and restructuring its debt to improve liquidity.
A new partnership with Georgina Energy signals a strategic pivot toward a potentially higher‑margin segment.
Recent AGM results and an investor presentation indicate the board is actively communicating its turnaround plan.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Cautiously optimistic: investors see a fresh start but remain wary of past management issues.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bullish chatter highlights the move to Georgina Energy as a ‘great move’ and praises the company’s willingness to cut losses and focus on new opportunities.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bear voices point to the repeated asset sales and debt restructuring as signs of a company that may never regain scale, warning that the market may still view the stock as a risk‑laden play.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Earlier posts were skeptical, but the latest pivot announcement has shifted the tone toward cautious optimism, though overall engagement remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat – no recent search spikes, meaning the market is still unaware of any upcoming catalysts.

near_term_catalysts: The next investor presentation (scheduled for early Q4) could reveal new funding or a breakthrough exploration finding.
A successful signing of a supply contract or a positive drilling result would provide a tangible catalyst.
If the company announces a new GM or senior management change, that could reset sentiment.
A surge in trading volume above the 30‑day average that supports a key support level would be a technical trigger.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals to monitor: (1) any announcement of new capital raising or loan agreements; (2) a confirmed drilling milestone; (3) a sustained volume spike that confirms support; (4) any mention of a new strategic partnership beyond Georgina Energy.
expect_next.timing_regime: The share appears to be in the early stages of a deep crash – capitulation seems complete, but the mean‑reversion cycle has not yet begun. The APEX compression score suggests a tight spring; once a catalyst confirms that the company can execute its pivot, a bounce is likely.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock has plunged over 70% and the company has just restructured its debt and sold non‑core assets, cutting liabilities by a large margin. A successful pivot to Georgina Energy could unlock new revenue streams, and the historical record shows that deep crashes often lead to outsized rebounds. If the share recovers to about 50% of its pre‑crash level, upside is roughly 100% from the current price.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the restructuring fails to bring in new capital or the Georgina Energy partnership stalls, the company may still be stuck in a cash‑burn cycle. A failure to hit a new support level or a further decline could push the share to a 90% drop from the pre‑crash price, leaving a net loss of the entire investment.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: ~200% if the share rebounds to 2× the current price. Potential downside: ~70% if the company collapses further. The asymmetry (high upside, low downside) favours a long position if the catalyst materialises.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback to the most recent low if volume confirms support and the share stays above the 50‑day moving average. Size the position so that a 20% drop would hit your stop. Use a stop 10% below the entry to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for the Q4 investor presentation or a new drilling result. A volume spike of 50% over the 30‑day average that also confirms support would be the trigger to enter.
playbook.if_passing: If the company fails to secure new financing or misses its drilling milestones, consider exiting. No signs of imminent delisting or bankruptcy yet, so the default stance remains bullish on a deep‑crashed setup.

ai_insights.bottom_line: SOU.L’s steep crash and recent debt cleanup set the stage for a high‑reward rebound once its Georgina Energy pivot proves viable – a classic contrarian play with asymmetric upside and limited downside.
